newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: New York museum returns lost Cambodian treasures.
newsitem.headline: New York museum returns lost Cambodian treasures.

text.p: New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art returned on Monday two centuries-old sandstone heads from Cambodia's ancient Angkor civilisation that had been missing for years.
The finely sculpted pieces were handed back by Martin Lerner, curator of the museum's collection of south and southeast Asian art.

He told reporters they had once been held at a conservation centre set up in the northwest town of Siem Reap to protect treasures from the nearby Angkor-era (9th-15th Century) temples and it was not known how they ended up in the United States.

An early 10th Century head of Shiva had been donated to the museum in 1985, while Lerner spotted the smaller 11th century bust at a Sotheby's sale last year. The owner was persuaded to return it to Cambodia.

Lerner, who did not know if the two treasures had been stolen or sold legally, said they were depicted in a publication listing 100 ancient Khmer art works which Cambodian authorities were trying to trace and recover.
Temple theft is a major problem in Cambodia, with the valuable busts and statues smuggled out of the country and sold to private collectors around the world.
